rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A detailed study of Marchantia (liverwort) reveals a flat, dichotomously branched thallus with upper air cavities and lower rhizoids. Asexual reproduction occurs through gemma cups that release gemmae. Sexual reproduction involves antheridia (sperm) and archegonia (egg) at the base of the stalked reproductive bodies; fertilisation requires water.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Thallus: upper (air cavities + chambers) + lower (rhizoids + scales)
Gemmae: asexual, in gemma cups
Fertilisation: sperm (2 flagella) + egg (in archegonium) → zygote (2n) → sporophyte (dependent)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The thallus is NOT a true leaf or stem; it is a flattened gametophyte body.  ·  Rhizoids are single-celled (in liverworts) or multicellular (in mosses) filaments; they are NOT true roots (no xylem/phloem).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a fully labelled Marchantia thallus (air cavities, rhizoids, gemma cups, antheridia, archegonia).  ·  Gemmae (asexual) vs spores (meiotic) — a common distinction question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Marchantia thallus: upper surface (air cavities + photosynthetic chambers) vs lower surface (rhizoids + scales).  ·  Gemma cups: dome-shaped, with gemmae that splash out in rain to form new thalli.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Gemmae are asexual propagules; spores are meiotic products — they are different.  ·  The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte (absorbs nutrients through the foot); it does NOT photosynthesise independently in Marchantia.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Marchantia thallus: upper air cavities + lower rhizoids + scales.  ·  Gemma cups: asexual reproduction via gemmae.  ·  Antheridia (male) + archegonia (female) at the base of the stalked reproductive bodies.  ·  Fertilisation requires water (flagellated sperm).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Marchantia polymorpha is the most commonly studied liverwort in NEB laboratories.  ·  Mosses and liverworts are sensitive bio-indicators of air pollution, especially SO2.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: DETAILED BRYOPHYTE (Marchantia) STRUCTURE AND LIFE CYCLE.  ·  Thallus: flat, ribbon-like, dichotomously branched; upper surface with air cavities (photorespiration) + photosynthetic chambers; lower surface with rhizoids (anchorage + absorption) + scales.  ·  Gemma cups: dome-shaped, on the upper surface; contain gemmae (asexual, multicellular) that splash out and grow into new thalli.
